lines.text: Wednesday night, November 11th, 2026. In Santa Clara, the lights are still on in a boardroom.
lines.say: Wednesday night, November eleventh, 2026. In Santa Clara, the lights are still on in a boardroom.

lines.text: Should the man who built Nvidia still be allowed to run it?

lines: In just a few days, investors had wiped out hundreds of billions of dollars of the company's value. And betting markets gave him less than a one-in-eight chance of surviving the year.
If you missed part one, here is what happened.
On Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted in an email to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife.
The woman, according to reports, was Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspected of working for China, and whose former company had bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips.
Nvidia's board opened an investigation, and said it had no reason to believe any secrets were compromised.

lines.text: Then, on Wednesday, came a second report.

lines: The New York Times reported that Huang had also had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reported directly to him.
The paper cited five former employees. Nvidia and Powell did not respond to requests for comment.

lines.text: When the Times called Huang himself, he reportedly said: "I don't think you should be talking to me directly." Then he hung up.
lines.say: When the Times called Huang himself, he reportedly said, I don't think you should be talking to me directly. Then he hung up.

lines: A CEO dating someone who reports to him is a serious problem at almost any big company, even before the questions about spies.
Under Nvidia's rules, a majority of its eleven directors can remove the CEO, with or without cause. Every director except Huang is independent.

lines.text: The board hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton, and reportedly a former federal prosecutor, to investigate.
lines.say: The board hired the law firm Wachtel Lipton, and reportedly a former federal prosecutor, to investigate.

lines: Bloomberg reported it was also working with an outside firm to find possible replacements. Nvidia has no public succession plan.
Some analysts have named the chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as a possible interim chief.

lines.text: Investors did not wait for the decision.

lines: Nvidia's shares fell about seven percent over the week, then more than eight percent more in after-hours trading on Wednesday.
If that drop holds, the company will have lost roughly 600 billion dollars in value since the investigation began.
Rivals rose: AMD gained four percent, Broadcom three.

lines.text: And Nvidia reports its quarterly results on November 17th, giving the board very little time.
lines.say: And Nvidia reports its quarterly results on November seventeenth, giving the board very little time.

In Washington, lawmakers threatened to subpoena Huang if he refuses a closed-door briefing.
After last week's midterm elections, Democrats now control both houses of Congress, and are promising oversight.
Inside the government, the Treasury Secretary reportedly challenged the Commerce Department over why Megaspeed had not been labelled a possible national-security threat.
And President Trump said Huang told him he had no idea the woman was allegedly a spy.
As of today, the board has not announced a decision.
Huang has said he did not know the woman was allegedly a spy. And no one has been charged with anything.

lines.text: He built a company the whole world depends on. Whether he still gets to run it may come down to a single vote.
